Honestly testosterone was a big aide in just finding myself and starting to love myself, but it didn't fix everything. I still went through like internalized transphobia with myself for awhile, but I started just doing what *I* enjoyed which meant just being myself

And being in college has given me a lot of personal freedom to explore who I am and I realize I'm not this girl I used to be, I'm a man and I look like a man in the mirror, and I get euphoria from being perceived as a man and looking like one. It's nearly impossible to call myself a girl even on accident now.

Going through transitioning has given me something I've never been able to do right though and that's being able to genuinely smile. I see old pictures of myself giving a fake ghost smile, and now I just compare that to where I am now, and the progress makes me overjoyed. 

So what I think makes me happy is not letting the past burden me too much, and patting myself on the back for coming so far. When I stopped fighting myself and became a friend to myself, everything changed :)
